task.title: Configuring port mapping for Red Hat Quay
task.shortdesc: To reach your proof of concept Red Hat Quay registry by hostname, you can map container ports on the host and add a static IP and hostname to /etc/hosts.

context.p: You can use port mappings to expose ports on the host and then use these ports in combination with the host IP address or host name to navigate to the Red Hat Quay endpoint.

step.cmd: Enter the following command to obtain your static IP address for your host system:

info.codeblock: --- link/ether 6c:6a:77:eb:09:f1 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 192.168.1.132/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global dynamic noprefixroute wlp82s0 ---

step.cmd: Add the IP address and a local hostname, for example, quay-server.example.com to your /etc/hosts file that you use to reach the Red Hat Quay endpoint. You can confirm that the IP address and hostname have been added to the /etc/hosts file by entering the following command:
